sections.title: Section 2: Exact Street Mechanics, Tools & Numbers
paragraphs: Thomas's bid formula at the Secureframe summit is plain arithmetic: take the vendor cost, for example 250 units at $185 for $46,250, add packaging (MeND's minimum charge is $350), add any labeling cost and $250 if DCMA inspection applies, add freight only when the award is not FOB origin, then stack the profit on the subtotal and divide by quantity to get the bid price entered in DIBBS [v7nJCLRc0uo @ 00:38:23]. The target margin is 10 to 15 percent; bidders opening at 20 to 25 percent simply get underbid [v7nJCLRc0uo @ 00:10:01]. The bigger lever came when MeND stopped chasing a percentage and asked whether the $7,035 profit justified the work; if $6,500 or $6,000 would do, the lower bid price made MeND more competitive and produced far more awards [v7nJCLRc0uo @ 00:39:51]. The same logic powers MeND's informal cost breakdown template: material, material overhead, labor, and other direct costs roll up to manufacturing cost, then G&A and packaging, then a 6.75 percent profit, producing $50,895 across 195 pieces, or $261 a unit [Y895jCYSE5A @ 00:11:19]. Thomas sends that Excel sheet whenever an officer pushes back on price.

When an officer asks for traceability plus a 45 to 60 day quote extension, Thomas first confirms the vendor still holds the old price, since requests in February 2025 still referenced quotes pulled in June and July 2024, then resubmits the same quote in DIBBS. Every document goes over as a PDF, never a PNG, JPEG, or raw screenshot the government system may not display, and the vendor price is redacted unless the email forbids it; if Thomas charges $3 and pays $1.25, there is no reason to show the $1.25 [Y895jCYSE5A @ 00:05:27]. Replies go on the original email thread so the officer can trace the history. Acceptable proof includes the vendor's quote PDF with logo and manufacturer part number, a branded Word quote, or the vendor's pricing email with signature. Counteroffers are negotiable: the officer anchors on the last purchase price plus inflation, and MeND answered one by blaming raw-material scarcity rather than a 3 percent CPI, attaching an informal cost breakdown [Y895jCYSE5A @ 00:09:47]. On another, a $3 bid met a $1.50 counteroffer and settled at $2.50. Go-to-Market Solutions flags the clause to check before pricing: FOB origin shifts risk to the government at the UPS scan, while FOB destination leaves damage and freight on the seller [szkqa7FwjYE @ 00:01:07].

Award decoding is a checklist Thomas runs on every DLA award before a purchase order goes to the vendor [sG-wAF0b7kQ @ 00:03:44]. Box 7 names the administrator: DLA appears on destination-inspection awards, while DCMA should appear when inspection is at origin. If the facility box in box 9 is blank, inspection happens at destination; if it holds a CAGE code, inspection happens at that location before anything ships. The PR number ties the award back to the RFQ, and its prefix flags the contract type: a PR starting with '100' marks an indefinite delivery contract, while '700' or '090' marks a standalone buy for an exact quantity [sG-wAF0b7kQ @ 00:15:16]. Thomas's IDC example showed a flat $250,000 on page one that was only the maximum value, with 2,712 guaranteed pieces, four estimated orders of at least 2,260 each, a $31 unit price, 175-day delivery, and packaging in groups of 25; nothing ships until a delivery order arrives. Go-to-Market Solutions says inspection at your own CAGE location must be requested in the bid with facility address, then confirmed on the award, with a call to the contracting officer if it is unclear [szkqa7FwjYE @ 00:03:13].

callout.title: Field Moves That Win the Paperwork Fight
callout.body: Four plays the speakers run to hold price, build supplier leverage, cut claim costs, and harden certificate files.
items: Refuse a counteroffer when the math does not work: MeND has told officers this is our price, do what you want, and still won the award, backing the number with an Excel informal cost breakdown [Tris10 @ MeND — Y895jCYSE5A @ 00:08:22].
Turn every vendor no-bid into a phone call using the number in the email signature; one of MeND's biggest authorized partners started as a no-bid [Secureframe — v7nJCLRc0uo @ 00:54:07].

Negotiate surplus-fund counsel: Sheila turned down a $3,500 upfront attorney fee, then talked a local attorney from $2,500 down to $1,250 on contingency for the Cook County motion [Money Making Juggernaut — MmWoRR82S9g @ 00:05:06].

Go past bare good faith on New York ST-120s: run the buyer's EIN or certificate of authority number through the state vendor lookup to confirm business name and registered address [Matt Sokol Business — Y3GHPpoT08s @ 00:09:07].

sop_steps.title: Decode the award before issuing a vendor PO
sop_steps.action: Highlight contract number, award date, PR number, Box 7 administrator, and the facility box on page one.
sop_steps.detail: A blank facility box means destination inspection; a CAGE code means inspection at that site before shipping; a PR starting with 100 means an IDC with no quantity until a delivery order lands; flow sampling data and drawing revision letters to the manufacturer [Tris10 @ MeND — sG-wAF0b7kQ @ 00:03:03].

sop_steps.title: Answer traceability in PDF on the same thread
sop_steps.action: Reconfirm vendor pricing, convert the vendor quote or email to PDF, redact cost unless forbidden, and reply on the original email.
sop_steps.detail: The government system may not read PNGs, JPEGs, or small screenshots, and replying in-thread lets the officer trace the full history; resubmit the DIBBS quote if a 45 to 60 day extension is requested [Tris10 @ MeND — Y895jCYSE5A @ 00:05:11].

sop_steps.title: Build the bid price or counter from the cost stack
sop_steps.action: Add vendor cost, packaging, labeling, DCMA inspection, and freight when not FOB origin, then add profit and divide by quantity.
sop_steps.detail: Example: 250 units at $185 is $46,250, plus a $350 packaging minimum and $250 inspection, plus $7,035 profit; test whether the profit dollars justify the work and trim to win [Secureframe — v7nJCLRc0uo @ 00:38:23].

sop_steps.title: Lock the certificate file before the sale
sop_steps.action: Collect a complete certificate, check its stated reason against what the customer buys, and file it with the supporting invoices.
sop_steps.detail: Texas Rule 3.287 requires purchaser name and address, item description, exemption reason, signature and date, and seller name and address; keep it at least 4 years, since missing certificates must be produced within 90 days of written notice [Tax Expert Today — WZL5m9rfNSQ @ 00:03:37].

sections.heading: Where Practitioners Disagree & Alternative Playbooks
paragraphs: Pricing posture is the sharpest split in the DLA lane. Tristan Thomas of Tris10 @ MeND treats a contracting officer counteroffer as an opening move, not an order: the MeND team has told buyers this is our price, it is what it is, do what you want, and still won the award [Y895jCYSE5A @ 00:08:22]. When Tristan does bend, the play is to meet in the middle, answering a $1.50 government ask on a $3 bid with $2.50, and attaching an informal cost breakdown that blames a raw-material supply shortage rather than the 3% CPI logic the buyer used [Y895jCYSE5A @ 00:09:02]. On the Secureframe stage, the same operator argues the margin side: newcomers who open at 20 to 25 percent simply get underbid, and the sweet spot sits between 10 and 15 percent [v7nJCLRc0uo @ 00:10:01]. The bigger reversal came when the team stopped chasing a margin percentage and asked whether raw profit dollars, $7,035 in the worked example, justified the work; trimming that to $6,500 or $6,000 lowered the bid price and produced far more awards [v7nJCLRc0uo @ 00:39:33]. Delivery promises follow the same contrarian logic, because Tristan quotes the lead time the vendor can actually hit and has won awards quoting 300 days against a requested 25.

Fulfillment strategy splits sharply on who controls inspection and packaging. Go-to-Market Solutions pushes operators to take control up front: if you want DCMA inspecting at your own CAGE location, request it in the bid with your CAGE code and facility address, confirm the award actually lists it, and call the contracting officer instead of assuming [szkqa7FwjYE @ 00:03:13]. Tris10 @ MeND reads the same question straight off the finished award: a blank facility box means inspection at destination, while a CAGE code in that box means origin inspection before anything ships [sG-wAF0b7kQ @ 00:03:59]. On packaging, Tristan Thomas lays out two distinct playbooks for the Secureframe summit audience. ASM D3951 commercial packaging is low cost and something people can handle themselves, but newcomers should just bid, build vendor relationships, and outsource MIL-STD-2073 work and MIL-STD-129 labels, ideally shopping two or three packaging partners because many packaging houses charge an insane amount that kills competitiveness [v7nJCLRc0uo @ 00:44:36]. Tristan also flatly rejects the popular advice to mine RFQs 60 to 90 days old on the theory that nobody bid; according to DLA contacts, those stale listings are leftovers from internal reassignments nobody closed out, so the MeND team works newest-first and knocks them out one by one [v7nJCLRc0uo @ 00:20:44].

Sales tax certificate practitioners split on how much policing a seller owes and how forgiving the audit clock runs. Brian Greer of TaxConnex frames it as the buyer's job to hand over the exemption certificate, with the seller charging tax by default until one arrives and then checking customer name, state ID number, reason, date and signature [FPLS7VL_qTA @ 00:03:44]. Matt Sokol calls New York's good-faith standard somewhat loose: accept the ST-120, retain it on file, and you are covered, with a vendor lookup by EIN or certificate of authority number as an optional extra step [Y3GHPpoT08s @ 00:07:01]. The Sales Tax Sisters push harder, telling sellers to smell-test every certificate, toss one where a candy seller claims resale on a cash register, and verify exempt status in the Comptroller's searchable taxpayer database. They also say Texas lets a seller rehab a missing certificate inside an audit years later under increased scrutiny, while New York shuts the door 90 days after the transaction [uZA19ayitYY @ 00:16:30]. Tax Expert Today describes a tighter Texas clock: after written notice the seller has 90 days to produce certificates, later deliveries are rejected, and anything gathered once fieldwork begins is verified before it counts [WZL5m9rfNSQ @ 00:03:20].

sections.heading: Firsthand Failure Modes, Traps & Economics Checks
paragraphs: The most expensive DLA mistakes surface after the win. Tristan Thomas of Tris10 @ MeND admits that when the team won its first contract three months into bidding, nobody knew what to do with it, and every question to DLA came back as file a mod or call the contracting officer [sG-wAF0b7kQ @ 00:00:25]. The recurring client trap is the indefinite delivery contract: an award showing a flat $250,000 is only the maximum value, flagged by a PR number starting 1-0-0, with zero quantity until a delivery order arrives; the example guaranteed just 2,712 pieces, was issued October 5, 2023, and drew its first delivery order two weeks later [sG-wAF0b7kQ @ 00:14:13]. On the bid side, Tristan's Secureframe list of fatal mistakes opens with not reading the solicitation down to the asterisks, which hides who pays freight and what packaging applies, then trusting one supplier quote without tracking why bids were lost [v7nJCLRc0uo @ 00:45:32]. Go-to-Market Solutions sees the same blind spot in shipping: FOB terms hide in section F, section A or elsewhere, and on FOB destination the box, including any damage, belongs to the seller all the way to the government warehouse [szkqa7FwjYE @ 00:01:23]. Tristan adds that packaging can cost more than the physical part, which wrecks any bid priced on item cost alone.

Sales tax audits punish files that look complete but are not. The Sales Tax Sisters say a seller who explains exempt sales by saying a customer named John phoned in a claim will be laughed out of the room, and clients routinely file a customer's sales tax permit or a 501(c)(3) IRS letter as if it were a certificate, when neither substantiates a tax-free sale [uZA19ayitYY @ 00:12:48]. Tax Expert Today adds that a Texas certificate missing any of the five Rule 3.287 items is disallowed no matter when it was obtained, that knowing misuse runs from a class C misdemeanor below $20 to a second degree felony at $20,000 or more, and that sellers must keep certificates at least four years [WZL5m9rfNSQ @ 00:02:07]. TaxConnex describes the auditor's default move: any exempt line without a valid, current certificate is treated as taxable and assessed tax, interest and a penalty [FPLS7VL_qTA @ 00:03:01]. Matt Sokol lists New York's misuse penalties at 100 percent of the tax due plus a $50 penalty for each fraudulent certificate issued, with possible revocation of the certificate of authority [Y3GHPpoT08s @ 00:06:16]. Hands Off Sales Tax explains why vendors grow strict: the liability sits with the vendor, so a vendor can reject a certificate even when the buyer believes it is correct.

Surplus funds and export work carry their own firsthand traps. Money Making Juggernaut warns that Texas and Georgia non-judicial deals hide costs only the foreclosure attorney or trustee can see, including accrued interest, the cost of the sale and the trustee's commission, so due diligence on additional debt and liens has to come first [KdtNDjlE4WQ @ 00:01:03]. Sheila, a 20-year Chicago broker featured on the same channel, spent about eight months hunting one claimant with no phone number or address and another month before a cautious niece passed the contact along; on an earlier deal Sheila went to court acting as the attorney and the judge laughed and ruled Sheila could not be part of the case. The attorney fix had its own math problem: $3,500 up front felt too risky on a credit card, and a $2,500 fee made no sense against one claimant's $19,000, so Sheila negotiated $1,250 on contingency [MmWoRR82S9g @ 00:05:06]. On the export side, Go Ask David flags the deemed export, where showing controlled technical data to a colleague from Japan at a conference in Arizona still counts as an export [c89xP1NJIx0 @ 00:04:21], and Cleared Systems prices violations at hefty fines, criminal charges and loss of export privileges [tEbWiX3Z22A @ 00:01:31].

callout.title: Four Checkpoints Before Money or Paper Moves
callout.body: Each checkpoint comes straight from a loss, reversal, or near miss the practitioners hit firsthand. Clear all four before you quote, ship, release a tax-free sale, or sign counsel on a surplus claim.
items: Before quoting, read the PR number: 1-0-0 means an estimated IDC quantity, while 700 or 090 means a firm quantity you must supply [Tris10 @ MeND — sG-wAF0b7kQ @ 00:15:16].
Before answering a traceability request, re-confirm the vendor price, convert everything to PDF, and reply inside the same email thread [Tris10 @ MeND — Y895jCYSE5A @ 00:06:09].
Before releasing a tax-free sale, hold a complete, signed, dated certificate whose stated reason matches what the customer actually buys [Tax Expert Today — WZL5m9rfNSQ @ 00:03:37].
Before signing a surplus attorney, size the fee against the claimant share; $2,500 on $19,000 failed and $1,250 contingency worked [Money Making Juggernaut — MmWoRR82S9g @ 00:04:46].

chapters.pull_quote: Get the documentation upfront when everybody still likes each other. Sales Tax Sisters (uZA19ayitYY @ 00:15:59).
action_checklist: Download every solicitation and press Ctrl-F or Command-F for FOB, inspection, and DCMA before pricing a single line [Go-to-Market Solutions — szkqa7FwjYE @ 00:00:46].

Build an informal cost breakdown with your vendor covering material, material overhead, labor, other direct costs, G&A, packaging, and profit to defend your price on counteroffers [Tris10 @ MeND — Y895jCYSE5A @ 00:11:19].
Price bids from vendor cost plus packaging, inspection, and freight when the government is not paying, then divide by quantity and judge the profit dollars [Secureframe — v7nJCLRc0uo @ 00:38:23].
Follow every vendor quote email or no-bid reply with a phone call to the person in the signature block [Secureframe — v7nJCLRc0uo @ 00:53:55].

Order the grant deed copy for about $4, file the claim fast with ID, affidavit, and death certificate, then send the claimant the USPS tracking number and call the county [Overage Acquisition — X_Oq8vv4j_c @ 00:01:22].

Request fresh exemption certificates at least every couple of years, annually in Florida, and add management software once you pass roughly 1,000 exempt customers [TaxConnex — FPLS7VL_qTA @ 00:04:59].
